steps.label: Three Goals
steps.content:
Three Goals

Write

Write real Cambridge Pseudocode instructions using CALL Name(...).

Order

Put instructions in the order they must actually happen - buy before you plant.

Automate

Turn a sequence that works once into a machine that repeats it forever.

steps.label: CALL Syntax
steps.content:
CALL Syntax

A sequence is a list of instructions that run once each, top to bottom, in the order they are written.

CALL Buy("Carrot")
CALL SetPosition(1, 0)
CALL Plant("Carrot")
  • Running a built-in action is called a procedure call, written CALL Name(...).
  • Anything in brackets is an argument - extra information the action needs.
  • A sequence has no branching and no repeating yet - every line runs exactly once.
  • Order matters: you cannot plant a seed you have not bought yet.

steps.label: Independent Task: Two Seeds
steps.content:
Independent Task: Two Seeds

Write your own sequence from scratch. No walkthrough this time - work out the order yourself.

Requirement

Write a sequence that: buys a Potato seed, then buys a Tomato seed, then moves to position (0, 2), then plants the Potato (not the Tomato) there.

y9_algorithms_l5_do_now.feedback: It comes right before the action's name, e.g. CALL Buy(...).
A function gives back a value and is used inside an expression - it is never written with CALL in front.

y9_algorithms_l5_worked_check.feedback: SetPosition moves the cursor to a tile, counted from home.
You cannot plant a seed you have not bought yet.

y9_algorithms_l5_fill_blank.feedback: The sequence buys a seed then plants it, with no move in between - add CALL SetPosition(2, 0) after the Buy and before the Plant.

y9_algorithms_l5_independent.feedback: Check the order: buy the Potato, buy the Tomato, move to (0, 2), then plant the Potato specifically - not the Tomato.

y9_algorithms_l5_plenary.feedback: Every procedure call starts with CALL.
An instruction can depend on something an earlier instruction set up, like owning a seed before planting it.
